'''Michael Girard''' was a Decipher-era [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]] (Gold 120, Apache Junction, Az) and the first [[Player Support Advocate]] of the [[Players Committee]], named by Warren Holland on 25 January 2002.<ref name="pc1" /> His Squadron slot was marked Retired after Decipher's SWCCG run.

He started playing in Great Falls, Montana, winning a sealed-deck demo tournament run by [[James Lafferty]]. Girard was a finalist at the [[1998 Decipher World Championship]], listed as Mike Girard, and qualified through Tatooine Tempe from Apache Junction, Arizona.<ref name="pkt">[https://blog.categoryonegames.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/07/1998-World-Championship.pdf 1998 World Championship packet], Decipher / Kendrick Summers (20 November 1998). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195330/https://blog.categoryonegames.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/07/1998-World-Championship.pdf Internet Archive].</ref> At the event Girard played eventual champion [[Matt Potter]].<ref name="decsq-prof">[http://www.decipher.com/volunteers/squadrons/players/girardmichael.html Star Wars CCG Squadrons: Gold 120 profile], decipher.com. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000604073410/http://decipher.com:80/volunteers/squadrons/players/girardmichael.html Internet Archive]</ref> At DecipherCon 1999 he also played [[Young Jedi]], finishing 45th in YJ Qualifier #2 (Sealed Deck).<ref name="dc99yj02_2">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/YJ02_2.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Scores: YJ Qualifier #2 (Sealed Deck)], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010108185300/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/YJ02_2.html Internet Archive]</ref>

A blank place means no posted standings give the player's place.

Decipher recruited volunteer Squadron Members in the 1990s to promote SWCCG locally (tournaments, demos, player support). "FL" is printed on some slots in the surviving tables.

== Jedi Knights TCG ==

Girard playtested the [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]] (2001).<ref name="jkrules">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt ''Jedi Knights'' Trading Card Game rulebook (credits)], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010820125115/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt Internet Archive]</ref>

== Radio Free Decipher ==

On ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' Broadcast 112 (25 January 2002), [[Scott Gaeta]] said Girard had been a roving reporter for [[Game Players Network]], covering big tournaments, before joining the [[Players Committee]].<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=docK2vpQWUI&t=874s Broadcast 112 - Radio Free Decipher (25 January, 2002): Scott Gaeta on the SWCCG PC], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 13 May 2022), at 14:34. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-docK2vpQWUI Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 112 transcript]].</ref>

By July 2003 Girard was one of Decipher's ''Lord of the Rings'' TCG game developers, with Jeff Snyder. On ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' Broadcast 170 he said the two would give colour commentary on the Lord of the Rings World Championship finals at Gen Con/DecipherCon 2003. [[Mark Tuttle]] would call play-by-play.<ref name="rfd170">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U8RGjcu1hUM&t=256s Broadcast 170 - Radio Free Decipher (18 July, 2003): Mike Girard on World Championships], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 14 May 2022), at 04:16. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-U8RGjcu1hUM Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 170 transcript]].</ref>
